Series::repeat_interleave¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::repeat_interleave(std::int64_t repeats) const -> Series
Series::repeat_interleave(std::int64_t repeats, std::int64_t dim) const -> Series

What It Does¶

repeat_interleave() repeats each element repeats times in place, so [10, 20, 30] with repeats = 2 becomes [10, 10, 20, 20, 30, 30].

This is the counterpart to repeat(): repeat() tiles the whole block (ABCABC), repeat_interleave() expands each element next to itself (AABBCC).

  • Without dim, the series is flattened to 1-D first, then every element is interleaved.

  • With dim, each slice along that axis is repeated repeats times, growing that axis by the factor repeats and leaving the shape otherwise intact.

The result is a fresh materialized array.

Parameters¶

repeats (std::int64_t)

How many consecutive copies of each element (or each slice, with dim).

dim (std::int64_t, optional)

The axis along which to interleave. Omitted: flatten first, then interleave.

Returns¶

Series A contiguous array. With dim, axis dim has length size(dim) *     repeats; without it, the result is 1-D of length numel() * repeats.

Gradient¶

repeat_interleave() is differentiable. Each source element (or slice) feeds repeats consecutive outputs, so the backward sums the upstream gradient over those repeats positions.

Examples¶

Example 1. Each element doubled in place.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0}).repeat_interleave(2));

Output¶

Series(shape=[6], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[10.0000, 10.0000, 20.0000, 20.0000, 30.0000, 30.0000]

Example 2. dim = 0 repeats each row; dim = 1 repeats each column.

auto m = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});

std::cout << "dim 0:\n" << m.repeat_interleave(2, 0);
std::cout << "\ndim 1:\n" << m.repeat_interleave(2, 1);

Output¶

dim 0:
pluss::Series(shape=[4,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2],
  [1, 2],
  [3, 4],
  [3, 4]]
dim 1:
pluss::Series(shape=[2,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=8, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 1, 2, 2],
  [3, 3, 4, 4]]

Example 3. The backward sums each element’s gradient over its consecutive copies.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.repeat_interleave(2).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 2, 2]

Example 4. With per-copy weights the two copies of each element accumulate separately.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

auto weights = pluss::make_series({10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0, 60.0});
(x.repeat_interleave(2) * weights).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[30, 70, 110]

Element 0 fed outputs 0 and 1, so it collects 10 + 20 = 30; element 1 collects 30 + 40 = 70; element 2 collects 50 + 60 = 110.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Without dim the series is flattened first, so a 2-D input comes back 1-D. Pass dim to keep the rank.

  • The ordering is AABBCC, not ABCABC — for the latter use repeat().

  • The result is a copy, not a view.

Summary¶

repeat_interleave(repeats [, dim]) expands each element in place:

  • AABBCC ordering; grows one axis (or flattens, then the whole length)

  • always contiguous

  • differentiable, backward sums each source element’s gradient over its repeats consecutive copies

See Also¶

  • Series::repeat: tiles the whole block instead (ABCABC).

  • Series::expand: a zero-copy broadcast of size-1 axes.
